title: Reproducible ledger-based CI for model artifact pinning, canary validators, and safe rollback
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: onboarding new model artifacts and publishing performance profiles currently requires manual verification and ad-hoc pinning. This leads to unsafe promotions, occasional regressions, and poor auditability.

Goal: implement a reproducible, ledger-backed CI flow that produces verifiable artifact attestations, runs automatic canary validators (functional + perf), and only publishes performance profiles and pins model versions after passing canaries. The flow must support safe automatic rollback and provide audit logs for compliance.

High-level design summary:
- Build pipeline computes canonical artifact fingerprint (content-addressable hash) and creates a signature envelope signed by the CI signing key.
- A lightweight "repro ledger" microservice records entries: artifact hash, provenance (git commit, builder image, deterministic build args), signature, build toolchain fingerprint, timestamp, and optional reproducibility metadata. Ledger entries are immutable and reference the artifact in the artifact store.
- Canary validators are triggered by a ledger entry: they run a small, reproducible workload (sample prompts, perf harness) across targeted runtime variants (float16/quantized) and evaluate correctness and latency/cost metrics.
- On canary pass, CI automatically publishes a signed performance profile into the profiles registry and creates a pin in the release broker tied to the ledger ID. If canary fails, CI marks the ledger entry with failure flags and leaves it in pending for manual inspection.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for this ticket to be Done):
1) CI produces a ledger entry for each model build containing artifact hash + signature + reproducibility metadata.
2) Canary validators run automatically and produce a machine-readable report (pass/fail, P50/P95 latencies, token cost delta).
3) Successful canary auto-promotes: signed performance profile published, model version pinned in release broker, and rollout plan created.
4) Auto-rollback trigger exists: if runtime metrics exceed thresholds (configurable: default P95 latency +30% or error rate >1%), the rollout is reversed and the pin is deactivated.
5) All steps produce auditable logs (console, cloud storage) and links to PRs/artifacts.
6) Security review (KMS usage, signer rotation, least-privilege artifact store) completed.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Stronger attestation and canary checks increase onboarding cycle time. We'll optimize by running perf checks on a sampling of representative inputs and caching intermediate KV states to reduce runtime cost.
- Using a ledger allows post-hoc verification and reduces silent promotions, but requires storage and retention policy decisions. We'll start with 90-day default retention for ledger entries and extend for enterprise customers.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A: prototype ledger + CI hooks in experimental project (internal-only).
- Phase B: wire validators to our canary infra and add auto-promotion to a test release-broker namespace.
- Phase C: enable for real onboarding pipelines behind a feature flag; iterate on thresholds and monitoring.

Notes: must coordinate with Security (KMS usage and signer rotation plan), Release team (release broker API changes), and DevX (docs/SDK for ledger verification).
implementation_notes: Add 'repro-ledger' microservice (immutable entries, indexed by ledger_id)
CI: build -> canonicalize artifact -> compute hash -> sign with CI signing key -> upload artifact -> write ledger entry -> emit ledger_id to pipeline
Trigger canary job that consumes ledger_id and pulls the artifact via the signed envelope, then runs functional and perf validators
Canary validators return a structured JSON report; CI parses report and decides pass/fail based on configured thresholds
On pass: publish signed performance profile to profiles registry (include ledger_id) and create pin in release broker via API call; create rollout and notify channels
On fail: attach report to ledger entry, tag as 'canary-failed', notify build owner and create a quick-repro run link
Implement auto-rollback job: monitor rollout metrics for the first 30 minutes (configurable); trigger rollback and unpin if thresholds breached
Integrate audit logs into console and forward to long-term storage for compliance (linkable from release view)
Add CLI/SDK helpers for verifying ledger entries and signature envelopes (devx task)
